body:
The Dictionary could be typed.
(AFAIK you ran into some problems with it; it would still be nice to resolve it though)

```suggestion
	void _create_dialog_item_selected(bool p_is_cancelled, const Callable &p_callback);
```
Don't use `const` with primitive arguments.

Why not use `const Callable` like in other callbacks?

EDIT:
Also other methods use CONNECT_DEFERRED. I don't remember why tbh, but might be relevant.
Same here.

```suggestion
	_call_dialog_callback(p_callback, p_is_cancelled ? selected_type : "", "create dialog");
```
It's the same callback for both, so no reason to differentiate like this.

```suggestion
	const String selected_type = create_dialog->get_selected_type();
```
The method returns a String.

Also it would be nice to avoid calling `get_selected_type()` with `p_is_cancelled`, as it's not going to be used anyway.

Isn't there a more efficient way? .-.
Iterating Dictionary like this is super slow. Probably won't matter in this context, but still.
The first string is argument for currently selected type. Maybe we could expose it too; other dialog popup methods also have such argument.
The `get_key_at_index` method here is `O(n^2)` btw, so good to avoid
The getter seems unused, so it should be removed.
Same.
What's this for?

> The Dictionary could be typed. (AFAIK you ran into some problems with it; it would still be nice to resolve it though)

Yeah, but I'd wait for others who maintains the typed dictionary to solve the problem and then I'll make a new pr to transform all dictionaries into typed dictionaries (as long as their keys or values should be typed)
Well the problem is that adding type technically breaks compatibility, so we should do it swiftly.
Nvm, wait for someone to fix #100137 ...

`popup_create_dialog(const Callable &p_callback, const StringName &p_base_type, const TypedArray<StringName> &p_custom_type_blacklist, const Dictionary &p_custom_suffix)`

`void EditorInterface::_create_dialog_item_selected(bool p_is_cancelled, const Callable &p_callback)`
I also exposed the second and last parameter of the original call

+			<param index="6" name="type_suffixes" type="Dictionary" default="{}" />
+			<description>
+				Pops up an editor dialog for creating an object.
+				The [param callback] must take a single argument of type [StringName] which will contain the type name of the selected object or be empty if no item is selected.
+				The [param base_type] specifies the base type of objects to display. If you set this to "Resource", all items shown in the create dialog are derived from [Resource].
+				When the [param replace_mode] is [code]true[/code], the title of the dialog will be "Change Type of "%s"" instead of "Create New %s". The [param replace_type_name] specifies the name of the type to be replaced.
+				The [param type_blacklist] contains a list of type names, and the types in the blacklist will be hidden from the create dialog.
+				The [param type_suffixes] is a dictionary, with keys being [StringName]s and values being [String]s. Custom suffixes override the default suffixes which are file names of their scripts. For example, if you set a custom suffix as "Custom Suffix" for a global script type,
+				[codeblock lang=text]
+				Node
+				|- MyCustomNode (my_custom_node.gd)
+				[/codeblock]
+				will be
+				[codeblock lang=text]
+				Node
+				|- MyCustomNode (Custom Suffix)
+				[/codeblock]
+				Bear in mind that when a built-in type does not have any custom suffix, its suffix will be removed. The suffix of a type created from a script will fall back to its script file name. For global types by scripts, If you customize their suffixes to an empty string, their suffixes will be removed.
+				[b]Note:[/b] Trying listing the base type in the [param type_blacklist] will hide all children of the base type from the create dialog.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a372214a4a047ccf63d23c4406337b30e55ff60b/editor/editor_interface.cpp#L459-L461

No, I meant the argument I mentioned originally, for specifying currently selected type.

For a currently selected type, using the first string of the original method has nothing to do with its primary selection, because it's used for setting the text of search box, and then nothing else related to selecting a specified type.
Maybe we should add this manually in `pop_create_dialog()`? Or adding it in `create_dialog.cpp`?

The search box will filter and select the specified type, so it effectively acts like currently selected type. You can test this by using Change Type in Scene dock, it will always select the type of the node you are replacing.
